newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel says further budget cuts needed.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel says further budget cuts needed.

text.p: A senior Bank of Israel official said on Thursday that additional cuts in the 1997 budget were needed to get the economy back on track.

Leo Leiderman, head of the central bank's research department, said in a statement that without the cuts, "it will be very difficult for the Israeli economy to get back on a positive path of improvement in exports and the current account deficit in the balance of payments."

The parliament on Wednesday gave preliminary approval for the government's 1997 budget. Spending cuts in the 190.8 billion shekel budget amount to 4.9 billion shekels, but this is being challenged by coalition members who say the cuts would hurt low-income groups.

Gesher, a faction in the ruling Likud party led by Foreign Minister David Levy, dropped its opposition to the legislation in return for a letter from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu promising to consider additional budget changes before a final vote in parliament by year's end.
Leiderman expressed grave concern about the "uncertainty which has been created with regard to elements of the budget cut".
Netanyahu said he was committed to the overall size of the cuts but did not rule out changing certain aspects of the cuts.
